title: Duchy of Tuscia
capsule: The Duchy of Tuscia was a Lombard administrative and military unit covering much of central Italy (modern Tuscany and parts of Lazio), established following the Lombard invasion of Italy around 568–576 with its capital at Lucca. The duchy was governed by a succession of Lombard dukes, beginning with Gummarito (576–585), and served as a frontier buffer against Byzantine territory to the south and east. Charlemagne's conquest of the Lombard kingdom in 774 transformed the duchy into a Frankish dependency under the Regnum Italiae; it was reorganized as a margraviate after 797. The narrow 577–587 attestation window reflects the earliest documented ducal phase under clear Lombard sovereignty.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. The duchy's existence is well attested in Lombard law codes and Frankish annals, but its precise southern and eastern boundaries vis-à-vis Byzantine territory are debated and were probably fluid.
